Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 09-05-2017 in M.V.C.No.5850/2011 passed by the learned VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and XXXIII ACMM and Member MACT, Bengaluru, (SCCH 5) ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the ranks of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

The brief facts of the case are, on 30-1-2011 at 6.00 p.m., while the petitioner was walking by the side of Chickmagalur-Bellur Road, in front of Jr.College, motor cycle bearing No.KA.18.R.6475 dashed against him, due to which, he fell down and sustained injuries.
After taking treatment at Government Hospital Chickmagaluru, NIMHANS and Abhaya Hospital, Bangalore, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.12,85,060/- with 9% interest p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri Satish R. Girji, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri C. Shankara Reddy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that, petitioner was under hospitalized for more NC: 2024:KHC:37477 than three months, huge money was spent towards treatment and he Sri H S Mohammed vs Sri C T Krishna Murthy on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167770491/
2 being a stone cutter unable to work as before.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical evidence is placed through PW2 to explain whole body disability at 55.70%, he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.6,000/- per month only, future prospects on the income is not considered and no compensation was awarded towards loss of income during laid up period, the petitioner is under continuous treatment and future medical expenses awarded is not sufficient and sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner after the treatment has become normal and he has resumed his work.
Medical evidence only speaks of 50-70% of disability and same was considered by the Tribunal.
The compensation awarded towards pain and sufferings and loss of amenities is on the higher side.
In the absence of any proof of income, the Tribunal has rightly taken the NC: 2024:KHC:37477 income of the petitioner at Rs.6,000/- and that the compensation assessed is on the higher side.

It is further contended that no bank will offer interest at 9% p.a., but the Tribunal has awarded higher rate of interest and therefore, it calls for modification.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the material on record.
8. The insurance Company has admitted its liability and satisfied the award passed by the Tribunal.
The point is only regarding quantum of compensation.
9. In the accident the petitioner has sustained head injuries.
He was treated at Government Hospital, Chickmagaluru, NIMHANS and Abhaya Hospital, Bangalore, under hospitalization for about 22 days.
The medical bills produced before the Tribunal at Rs.3,33,500/- has been ordered to be reimbursed to the petitioner by the Tribunal.
PW2 Dr. Sharan Srinivasan, Neuro surgeon with the assistance of Neuro Psychologist assessed the disability of petitioner to an extent of 55.70%.
Nature of evaluation has been narrated in his affidavit and the cross- examination did not brought out anything.
Hence, the functional disability of the petitioner has to be treated at 55.70%.
The petitioner though claims that he was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m., he has not produced any document to prove his income.
In the year 2011, a person with no proof of income, would be earning not less than Rs.6,500/- per month and the same has to be taken accordingly.

Since the functional disability is above 50%, and petitioner is aged 40 years,
25% of his income has to be considered as future prospects for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
If that is so, the loss of future income will be Rs.6,500/- + 1,625/- (25%)=8,125/- x 12 x 15 x 55.70% =Rs.8,14,612/-.

11. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of NC: 2024:KHC:37477 amenities and discomforts and Rs.25,000/- towards incidental expenses such as, attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance and the same is kept in tact.

The petitioner will be laid up minimum of five months and loss of income during the said Sri H S Mohammed vs Sri C T Krishna Murthy on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167770491/
3 period comes to Rs.6,500x5= Rs.32,500/-.
12.

sentences.text: The medical evidence speaks that petitioner was to be under continuous treatment and he was advised to take AED (Anti Epileptic Drugs) and he has been regularly followed.
Hence, future medical expenses is inevitable.

Hence, it is to be assessed at Rs.50,000/- instead of Rs.20,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Total compensation comes to Rs.15,16,512/- instead of Rs.12,80,060/-
awarded by the Tribunal and thereby an enhancement of Rs.2,70,552/- which is rounded off to Rs.2,70,550/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Adverting to the rate of interest is concerned, it is contended on behalf of the insurance company that the Tribunal has not assigned any reasons for awarding higher rate of interest.
Perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has referred to the judgment of the Supreme court in para 27 of its judgment and awarded the interest.
The Tribunal did not discuss the factual circumstances of those judgments and not assigned any special reason to award interest at 9% p.a.
Since the insurance Company is not in appeal, it is not proper to interfere with the discretion of the Tribunal.

But insofar as enhanced compensation is concerned, the petitioner is entitled to the interest at 6%
p.a.
14.
